authorization: Maintainer decision 2026-09-17 answering open question Q1 of the dev Claude conversion: dev receives eval coverage, owned by the validator rather than carried inside the dev package. Authorizes adding the dev observation campaign to the Claude validator and rebinding its build manifest. Does not authorize a new grader or profile, changes to scripts/run_evaluation.py, running any campaign or test suite, or edits to the Codex validator under src/agents.
history_review: Prior authoring run 20260917T115002Z-review-fixes published AUTHORED with a verified publication readback; its authoring-baseline.json is bound as prior and its managed paths are the edit base. The target tree was restored to exactly those baseline bytes before this run was staged, verified by an empty recursive diff against that run's baseline directory.

requirements.outcome: The dev skill receives validator-owned eval coverage: a retained per-target case registry inside the validator package, matching how the validator retains its own and the builder's cases.

The campaign is discoverable: evals/README.md names the new file and states that it is an observation registry for bounded trials rather than grader input, so no reader expects a profile to execute it.

The runner's package binding still resolves: evals/build-manifest.json enumerates every package file except itself with a matching digest, because run_evaluation.py rejects the package when the actual file set differs from the manifest in either direction.
No executable campaign is created or altered: profiles, graders and scripts/run_evaluation.py keep their existing bytes and the profile and grader counts are unchanged.

capabilities: Python 3.10+ standard library for digest computation
expected_outputs: evals/dev-cases.jsonl holding D01-D20 in the validator-cases.jsonl observation shape
side_effects: An assessment that selects the dev skill now finds a retained case registry in the validator package
known_issues: D01-D20 are builder-authored declarative expectations derived from the dev package. They are not independently derived oracles: an assessor must still construct its own fixtures and expected results from the original dev requirements rather than treating this file as an answer key.

No deterministic grader campaign exists for dev. Adding one needs a new profile, a matching PROFILES entry in scripts/run_evaluation.py and a grader suited to assessing a product-implementation workflow. That is executable-campaign work and was deliberately not attempted. Recorded as design open question Q1.
The Codex validator at src/agents/skills/skill-validator did not receive this campaign, and the Codex dev package still has no eval coverage. Recorded as design open question Q2.

The validator's own unittest suite was NOT_RUN for these bytes; running it belongs to the validator's workflow, not to authoring. The package binding was instead verified read-only by recomputing every artifact digest and comparing the result with both the manifest and the published baseline.
